title: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI

claim.summary: WxCrop is an LLM assistant that routes plain-language questions to tools computing causally selected daily county hazard indices from weather records and forecasts and a payout-calibrated crop-loss model, assembling every reported number from tool receipts.

modules.name: Receipt-grounded tool answering
modules.scope_reason: Structured tool requests, receipts that carry value, unit, data version and filters, and replies assembled only from receipts with explicit refusal outside tool coverage would work unchanged for a non-temporal assistant.
evidence_locators: PDF p.27; passage beginning "From a question it writes a"
PDF p.27; passage beginning "The reply is then assembled by"

modules.name: Causally selected daily compound hazard indices
modules.scope_reason: Each index combines hazard-specific weather drivers per county and day (for hurricanes a wind load multiplied by a rainfall amplifier) with tiers anchored on insured crop-loss frequency, so its form and thresholds are selected for the agricultural hazard-assessment output.
evidence_locators: PDF p.7; passage beginning "Wind and rainfall mattered, and so"
PDF p.15; passage beginning "The study covers the 67 counties"

modules.name: Growth-stage-aware, payout-calibrated crop-loss model
modules.scope_reason: Expected loss per crop group combines the index with crop susceptibility and date-dependent growth-stage vulnerability and is calibrated by inverting insurance payouts, and the hazard tier gates whether it runs, so it is bound to the crop-loss output contract.
